There was no precedence of studies using continuous TCF, the interface compatibility, and whether the TCF had to be pre-heated to receive the SMC etc. These were systematically addressed in this study. Figure 70 illustrates the TCF as produced at the Carbon Fiber Technology Facility (CFTF) at ORNL. This TCF was cut to 6”x6” size and placed in the tool for overmolding with SMC. The position of the TCF can be either as the bottom most layer or in some cases sandwiched between 2 SMC charges, where the TCF become the center layer. The panel was molded at 1000 psi with 40 wt.% SMC charge. The glass side and the TCF side of the molded panel is shown in Figure 70 (middle, right), indicating a well-consolidated panel. 52 Figure 70. (Left) TCF produced at the CFTF was cut and placed in a 6”x6” mold. (Middle) Glass SMC side of the over molded panel; (Right) TCF side of the over molded panel The TCF-glass SMC panel(s) were evaluated with ultrasonic pulse echo phase array method using an Olympus ultrasonic equipment conducted with a 5 MHz transducer. Figure 71 illustrates the reflected signals observed on the oscilloscopes. Based on the gate settings, the layers were observed effectively including the TCF-SMC layer. This can be seen clearly in Figure 71 The ultrasonic evaluation also provides indication of TCF movement and shifting (if any) in the stack. Figure 71. Ultrasonic pulse-echo phase array evaluation of the TCF-glass SMC panel. (Top left) Ultrasonic reflected pulses and gate settings; (Top right) close up of the panel through the thickness observed in ultrasound; (Bottom) Full field ultrasonic scan where the TCF is clearly observed at the location of the arrow. Flexural testing was conducted for ‘along’ and ‘across’ directions where the glass SMC was in the MD but with the TCF on the tension side. The SMC was tested in the MD (along) and CD (across). Figure 72 compares the flexural strength for the SMC by itself and SMC over molded with TCF for the ‘along’ and ‘across’ direction. Figure 72 does the same for flexural modulus. 53 The SMC by itself has an average flexural strength of 335 MPa while the TCF over molded SMC was ~ 17% higher than the constituent SMC. The ‘along’ direction over molded specimen was 439 MPa compared to ‘across’ 373 MPa respectively. The average flexural modulus was 11.4 GPa for the SMC by itself. The flexural strength of the over molded TCF was 10-31% higher than constituent SMC. The flexural modulus of the over molded TCF SMC was 84%- 116% higher (20.94 GPa for across, and 24.64 GPa for along) than constituent SMC. Figure 72. Comparison of flexural strength and flexural modulus for the constituent SMC and TCF over molded SMC for the ‘along’ and ‘across’ directions. The over molded specimens exhibited 10-31% increase in flexural strength and 81-118% increase in flexural modulus.
